reviewContext.userProblem: vactr resolves notes only through fixed 12-TET (src/sched/commit.rs:43 note_to_freq), and its 17 named scales are 12-tone only. It has chord, voicing and arp, but no strum, harp or chord-performance helper. The user asked for FM-1-inspired microtonal tuning and strum/harp chord performance, using the synth concepts only (no GPL firmware code).
requiredOutcomes: Tuning model: n-EDO (steps 1..=1200, covering 5..53), non-octave EDO periods (Bohlen-Pierce 13 steps of 3:1), JI ratio lists, inline and loaded Scala .scl text with optional .kbm, and presets :ji-5 :ji-7 :partch-43 :bohlen-pierce plus 11 microtonal scale presets (plan 01).
The tune combinator and the strum, harp and inversion pattern nodes (hash tags 43-46), with explicit arms in every exhaustive PatNode match, including song freeze and timing capture (plan 02).
Tuned frequency resolution at audio commit, MIDI commit (nearest 12-TET note), song freeze and song encode. Untuned output stays bit-identical (plan 03).
Tuning-aware scale, chord and voicing, with microtonal scale presets accepted by scale (plan 04).

Nine natives (tune edo ratios scala load-scala strum harp inversion perform) appended to the DOMAIN table, which also supplies completion and hover metadata, plus scheduler and song end-to-end tests (plan 05).
A lang-reference.md section 6 and runnable examples/microtonal-tuning.vact and examples/strum-harp.vact (plan 06).

Full gates under the measurement lock: build, strict clippy, fmt, full nextest, wasm --lib and release-wasm, npm check, vitest, frontend build and test:style. Invariant checks and an impl-plans/README.md entry (plan 07).

designDecisionsAndRationale: D1: with no tuning, the exact existing code paths run (note_to_freq, integer scale/chord/voicing, MIDI rounding), so the default is bit-identical by construction.

D2: a tuning spec is a dict value. On events it travels as the 'tuning' control in a canonical list form ([:edo ..] or [:degrees ..]), so it freezes into song mode as FrozenControl::List without codec changes.
D3: tune is control-like (chord shape) and gives no structure to an unstructured subject unless the tunings pattern is structured.
D4: key root (default 60) is degree 0 and sounds at note_to_freq(root). ref-key and ref-freq override the anchor (TQ2).
D5: frequency resolution runs only on the scheduler side; the audio thread still receives f32 constants.
D6: MIDI out under a tuning sends the nearest 12-TET note of the tuned frequency, with no pitch bend (TQ1).
D7: 12-tone vocabularies map into a tuning by the nearest-key rule, and apply directly when K == 12.
D8: no permissive upstream is used, so THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md is unchanged.
D9: new public names are tune, edo, ratios, scala, load-scala, strum, harp, inversion and perform.
intentionalTradeoffs: Tuned var-driven notes commit Ctl::Const frequencies instead of CellMap::NoteToFreq cells, so live retuning of held notes is deferred (TQ4).
MIDI loses up to 50 cents of microtonal deviation (nearest-note policy).
strum time must be exact (Int/Ratio). A Float is a Type fault that suggests a ratio such as 1/32.
Live MIDI input lanes do not support the new operators. walk keeps its 'cannot re-time live input' reject.
perform composes chord > voicing > inversion > mode and has no PatNode of its own.
supportedEdgeCases: Fractional keys interpolate in log frequency. If either neighbor is unmapped, the result is no tone.
A .kbm 'x' entry (unmapped) drops that tone with no fault. An unmapped reference key is a Type failure.
Scala input with \r\n line endings, comments, and trailing text after values.
Microtonal scale presets on untuned events insert their EDO tuning control without overwriting an existing recognized tuning.
A non-default root (root: :d) anchors note names at ROOT (DR-2). Under 19-EDO, :d is key 63 by default (DR-1).
strum time is clamped (dt = min(time, len/N)). :alternate follows parity, and :random is a deterministic Fisher-Yates.
harp pos is clamped to [0, 1] and evaluated per event; strips outside 1..=64 is a constructor Type failure.
inversion with negative and multi-period n, and the bass flag.
An unrecognized tuning control value (for example Int 3) keeps today's instrument-parameter handling.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: MPE or per-channel pitch-bend MIDI output.
Live retuning of already-sounding var-driven notes.
New strum, harp or inversion behavior on live MIDI input lanes.
load-scala on hosts without a SourceLoader (fails with host-unavailable).
